text: Document-editor Refactor Plan (3/3) — Gateway, Issues, Project, Phases

text.text:
Replaces nginx. Hosts the auth issuer and the reverse-proxy.

• *Auth issuer* — RS256 JWTs, JWKS endpoint, RS256 signing, internal-service-token for upstream calls
• *Reverse-proxy* — `httpx.AsyncClient` forwarding `/api/v1/{svc}/*` → upstream per service-discovery table
• *WebSocket proxy* — `fastapi.WebSocket` with manual upstream stream forwarding
• *Realtime push* (optional) — RabbitMQ → Server-Sent Events (`/api/realtime/sse?topics=...`)
• *Rate limiting* — Redis token-bucket keyed by user-id and route-prefix
• *Idempotency* — Redis-backed `Idempotency-Key` cache, replays previous response
• *Caching* — read-through Redis for `/api/rooms`, `/api/documents`
• *Observability* — OpenTelemetry to collector, mirrors Rust tracing

*M0 Foundations* (10) — bootstrap all 9 crates + root workspace
*1.* [infra] root umbrella Cargo workspace
*2-10.* [packages] domain, contracts, errors, observability, auth, cache, persistence-postgres, persistence-mongo, messaging-rabbitmq

*M1 Containers* (7)
*11-17.* docker-compose, Dockerfiles, RabbitMQ topology, healthchecks, `.env.example`, `.gitignore`

*M2 Gateway (Python)* (9)
*18-26.* FastAPI bootstrap, JWT issuer, reverse-proxy, WS proxy, rate-limit, idempotency, correlation, RabbitMQ→SSE, smoke tests

*M3 room-service* (6)
*27-32.* bootstrap, RoomManager→Mongo+outbox, publish room.* events, WS + CRDT, subscribe document.commit.recorded, testcontainers tests

*M4 doc-service* (6)
*33-38.* bootstrap, DocumentManager→Postgres+outbox, wire TextDocument CRDT, publish document.* events, subscribe latex.compile.succeeded, CRDT property tests

*M5 latex-service* (6)
*39-44.* bootstrap, move `backend/src/latex`, subscribe `latex.compile-requested`, publish `latex.compile.{succeeded,failed}`, store artefacts + metadata in Mongo, bake texlive

*M6 E2E parity + cutover* (3)
*45-47.* Re-implement existing APIs behind gateway; update frontend vite proxy; cutover compose

*Project*: `Document-editor — Backend Refactor`
*Template*: Team backlog

*Custom fields*
• `Status` — Backlog / In Progress / In Review / Blocked / Done
• `Track` — Foundations / Infra / Gateway / Backend·room / Backend·doc / Backend·latex / E2E
• `Priority` — P0 / P1 / P2 / P3
• `Estimate` — S / M / L / XL
• `Milestone` — linked milestones M0..M6
• `Area + Tracks` — labels

*Views*
1. *Table* — Title | Status | Track | Priority | Milestone | Owner | Estimate
2. *By Milestone* — board M0..M6
3. *By Track* — board by Track
4. *Critical Path* — P0+P1, status ≠ Done
5. *Roadmaps* — Timeline grouped by Track

```
Phase 0  (now)        create issues + project
Phase 1  (~2d)        M0  — all 10 crates + contracts schema
Phase 2  (~2d)        M1  — compose + Rabbit topology
Phase 3  (~5d)        M2  — Python gateway MVP (proxy + JWT)
Phase 4  (~5d)        M3  — room-service parity
Phase 5  (~5d)        M4  — doc-service + wire-in CRDT
Phase 6  (~3d)        M5  — latex-service parity
Phase 7  (~2d)        M6  — frontend cutover, deprecate legacy
```
Each phase ends with feature-parity tests in `tests/e2e/`, all green, PR merged into `refactor/backend-services`. `master` untouched.

1. *WS through gateway* adds latency — alternative is Traefik rules routing WS directly to services
2. *axum vs actix-web* — switching to `axum` for cleaner `tokio`+`lapin` integration
3. *MongoDB scope* — proposed: room snapshots + latex artefact metadata
4. *Migrations* — sqlx per-service folders vs single root set
5. *Auth issuer* — Python gateway owns user creation too, or split into Rust `auth-service` (like RPBI `identity-service`)?
